title: Transient heat in a bar (NAFEMS T3)
sentence: A bar driven by a sinusoidal surface temperature and held at zero at the other end — the θ-method marching in time.

expected.quantity: T 20 mm inside the driven face at t = 32 s

theory: Transient conduction $\rho c_p \dot T = \nabla\cdot(k\nabla T)$ is marched by the $\theta$-method: $\left(\mathbf{C} + \theta\,\Delta t\,\mathbf{K}\right)\mathbf{T}^{n+1} = \left(\mathbf{C} - (1-\theta)\,\Delta t\,\mathbf{K}\right)\mathbf{T}^{n} + \Delta t\,\mathbf{f}$. $\theta = 0.5$ is Crank–Nicolson, second-order accurate and unconditionally stable; $\theta = 1$ is backward Euler, first-order but free of the oscillation Crank–Nicolson can show at a step change. The Step runs in kelvin above the initial state, which is the same problem: linear conduction is invariant under a shift of the whole field.
